items.what: The copy gate silently skips any ns.L entry not shaped `NAME = value` (e.g. a bracketed key `["B"] = "..."`), so its banned-word, stray-percent and "?" checks never run on it and the gate still passes
items.why: Verified: strings_table(tokenize('ns.L = { A = "ok", ["B"] = "the fastest route" }')) returns only A; the banned 'fastest' passes unreported. Lua allows the bracketed form, so the gate would pass on a shape it cannot read. phrases.py:41 has the same skip, so the same entry would also drop out of Locales/phrases.txt without warning. Raising ValueError on an unrecognised entry shape, as strings_table already does for a missing table, makes the gate fail instead. No such entry exists in Locales/enUS.lua today.
items.reason: strings_table raises on an ns.L entry not shaped NAME = value

items.quote: start = next(i for i in range(len(texts) - 4) if texts[i : i + 5] == ["ns", ".", "L", "=", "{"])
items.what: phrases.phrases (tools/phrases.py:35-46) re-implements locating and walking the ns.L table that lint_copy.strings_table (tools/lint_copy.py:85-102) already does: find the `ns . L = {` token run, take the body up to matching(), split on ',', skip entries without '='. Canonical home: lint_copy (phrases already imports matching/split/unquote from it); expose one helper yielding (key token, value tokens) per ns.L entry and let each caller apply its own value rule.
items.why: Both parse Locales/enUS.lua's ns.L with the same five-token search and the same entry filter, copied line for line. Differences: (1) a missing table raises ValueError('no ns.L = { ... } table') in lint_copy but a bare StopIteration in phrases (accidental drift); (2) value handling differs on purpose: lint_copy splits on 'or' and joins every literal of each alternative (so it lints both sides of `GLOBAL or "x"` and nested tables), phrases requires every '..' piece to be a single string literal (so GlobalString fallbacks are left out of the template). Only the table-location and entry-walk part is duplicated; a change to how ns.L is declared (e.g. `local L = {}` then `ns.L = L`) must land in both.

items.what: tools/screenshots.py (1335 lines) holds separable responsibilities: the anchor resolver (45-178, already tested alone); the headless scene runner and layout pass (180-242); wowmock/font loading and text fitting (244-304); stock-template recipes and STOCK (306-557); the Layout compositor (560-789); the world-map frame and pins (791-927); Shortest Path's route: fetching/extracting an SPF checkout at a pinned sha, the UiMapAssignment projection, running Path.FindSync under LuaJIT, breadcrumbs and goal pins (929-1157); manifest, demo GIF and the scene script render() (1159-1335).
items.why: The file is sectioned and single-purpose (make screenshots), so size alone is not the defect; but the SPF route section is a self-contained subsystem (external repo fetch/cache, its own pin SPF_SHA, git archive / tarball fallback, a Lua program string, map projection) that no other section touches except via shortest_path(). A change to SPF's pin or its drawing never touches the resolver or recipes. Proposed split: tools/screenshots_spf.py (929-1157 plus sibling()), optionally tools/screenshots_stock.py for the recipes (306-557); the resolver could move with its tests. Low urgency: not a god file, and no dead code to remove first.
items.reason: The oversized-modules exception for one coherent responsibility applies: these sections form one headless screenshot pipeline. The proposed SPF subsystem shares map, font, texture and wowmock helpers with the other scenes, and manifest() consumes SPF_SHA, so its claimed isolation behind shortest_path() does not hold.

items.what: screenshots.map_position (tools/screenshots.py:1014-1020) re-derives the world (north, west) -> uiMap (x, y) projection that gen_quests.project (tools/gen_quests.py:231-244) owns, with the same UiMapAssignment Region_1/Region_4, Region_0/Region_3 and UiMin/UiMax arithmetic. Canonical home: gen_quests.project (gen_zoneart.py already imports from gen_quests); screenshots could call project(assignment(ui, map_id), x, y).
items.why: Same formula, same DB2 columns, both read wago.tools rows as string dicts. Differences: project bounds-checks (point inside the Region box, a non-degenerate region, result in 0..1) and returns None otherwise; map_position extrapolates without checks. That difference would need checking for walk points just outside the zone rect (Path.FindSync may step off the uiMap rect), so a switch must handle None. world_point (1003-1011) is the inverse and has no counterpart in gen_quests. The docstring says the math inverts 'SPF's projection', a third copy in another repo.
items.reason: The contracts differ: map_position selects a row for a 2-D point and extrapolates, raising on degenerate spans, whereas project accepts a supplied row and altitude and returns None for out-of-region, degenerate or off-map points. Pinned SPF 061f0b1 Route.lua:88-118 preserves off-map endpoints for segment clipping, AGF map_frame clips after drawing, and a cached Barrens-row probe produced (-0.1, 0.5) versus None, establishing a rendering constraint that requires this divergence.
